text:
Zoe: quick heads-up — i put together a tiny proposal for telemetry merge/window priority buckets. goal: keep late-enrich traces from spiking hot paths and budget, while preserving queryability for short windows. thoughts?
Rohan: can you sketch the buckets? low/high or more granular?
Zoe: initial idea: 3 buckets — realtime (high), delayed (medium, 1-12h), archival (low, >12h). delayed gets lightweight envelope with minimal attrs, archival is compacted.
Priya: so delayed would still allow tail-latency debugging, correct? how do we ensure we can stitch to full spans later?
Zoe: yes — plan is to keep canonical trace id + sample markers in delayed envelope. stitcher service reconstructs on-demand using compact pointers into archival storage.
Rohan: sounds good but worried about cost attribution. If we compact and drop tokens, how do we calculate cost per-tenant?
Priya: we can propagate billing_key through envelope and keep a tiny billing delta record in delayed bucket. cheaper than full enrichment.
Zoe: exact — billing_key + coarse token counts. also keep a checksum to verify reassembled payload.
Rohan: fallback policy? if stitcher fails or latency-sensitive query needs full data, do we fallback to re-run enrich pipeline (expensive)?
Zoe: fallback order: 1) try reconstruct from delayed+archival fast path, 2) if missing, queue a rehydrate job (best-effort, delayed), 3) surface degraded result to caller with reason code.
Priya: can we avoid rehydrate queues triggering huge loads? maybe rate-limit and per-tenant quotas.
Zoe: yep — per-tenant rehydrate budget + global smoothing window. also we can prioritize by SLA tier.
Rohan: how would this affect tracing query UX? devs expect full spans in traces UI for recent incidents.
Zoe: for recent (realtime bucket) no change. delayed shows synthetic placeholder with link "reconstruct" that triggers stitcher; for most incidents stitcher returns quickly.
Priya: any change to ingest contract? sounds like we need small schema: {trace_id,billing_key,timestamp,attrs_min,checksum,priority_bucket} — can we keep it backward compatible?
Zoe: we add optional fields; no required change for edge producers. enrichment/ingest will map to bucket based on heuristics (latency, tenant config).
Rohan: metrics/alerts: we'll need SLOs for rehydrate latency and reconstruction success rate. also costs per bucket for chargebacks.
Zoe: agreed — will add dashboards: rehydrate-rate, success-rate, avg-latency, cost-by-bucket.
Priya: implementation workstreams?
Zoe: 1) ingest router — classification & envelope emit (small change), 2) compact archive format + index, 3) stitcher service + API, 4) Console UX and billing pipeline hooks. estimate: 6-8 sprints across teams if prioritized.
Rohan: can we pilot with 2 tenants and one non-prod region?
Zoe: yes — propose pilot with a low-volume internal tenant and one willing customer. I'll draft an RFC and include a migration playbook.
Priya: :thumbsup: ping me on the RFC draft.
ObservabilityBot: Scheduled follow-up meeting created: #telemetry-merge-pilot Weds 10am.
Zoe: thanks — adding notes + action items to the RFC.
Rohan: nice work, Zoe.
Priya: ok, dropping off — we'll iterate on billing details in the doc. :v:
